module_title: Population Density and Growth - Basic Understanding & 2011 Data
introduction: A country's population is not just a numbers game; it reflects the pressure on the nation's land and resources. The Census is conducted every 10 years (under the Ministry of Home Affairs). At this level, we will memorize the most foundational and frequently asked statistics regarding 'Population Density' and 'Decadal Growth'.

core_concepts.title: What is Population Density?
core_concepts.description: Population density is defined as the 'average number of persons living per square kilometer of area' (Formula: Total Population ÷ Total Area). According to the 2011 Census, India's national population density is '382 persons per square kilometer' (up from 324 in 2001).

core_concepts.title: States with Highest and Lowest Density
core_concepts.description: 'Bihar' is the most densely populated state in India (1,106 persons/sq km), closely followed by West Bengal (1,028). On the opposite end, 'Arunachal Pradesh' has the lowest population density in the country (only 17 persons/sq km).

core_concepts.title: Decadal Population Growth Rate
core_concepts.description: This metric shows the percentage increase in population over a period of 10 years (between two censuses). India's Decadal Growth Rate between 2001 and 2011 was '17.72%'.

core_concepts.title: States with Highest and Lowest Growth
core_concepts.description: 'Meghalaya' recorded the highest decadal growth rate (27.9%) between 2001-2011. The most shocking and unique statistic came from 'Nagaland', which recorded a 'Negative' growth rate (-0.6%).

important_entities.name: Nagaland
important_entities.key_fact: The ONLY State with a Population Decline
important_entities.significance: In the 2011 Census, Nagaland was the absolute only state in all of India to record a negative decadal growth rate (-0.6%). This means it actually had fewer people in 2011 than it did in 2001. This single fact has been asked in countless exams.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: This is the most common beginner mistake. If an exam asks: 'Which state has the highest Population?' the answer is 'Uttar Pradesh'. But if it asks: 'Which state has the highest Population Density?' the answer is 'Bihar'. Density means crowding, not total numbers.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember B-A: B for Bihar (Highest Density), A for Arunachal (Lowest Density).

exam_strategy_tips: India's national population density ('382') and national decadal growth rate ('17.72%') must be rote-memorized. They are asked directly.
Always read the question carefully to see if it is asking for a 'State' or a 'Union Territory'.
